summary:
The Monkey D. Luffy manga alternate art numbered OP05-119 sits in the part of the One Piece Card Game catalogue where the artwork, not the gameplay, is the entire proposition. Manga-art parallels drop the painted illustration style used across ordinary printings and replace it with black-and-white panel linework borrowed from the language of the comic itself. For Luffy - the character whose silhouette carries the whole franchise - that treatment turns a card into something closer to a framed manga page, and the 119 slot has become shorthand among collectors for the highest-attention art chase in its block.

### Basic Info
*   **Main subject / card theme:** Monkey D. Luffy, captain of the Straw Hat Pirates
*   **Set or product (catalog label):** 2023 Awakening of the New Era Manga Alternate Art
*   **Card number:** OP05-119
*   **Language version(s):** English catalog entry
*   **Rarity / treatment:** Manga alternate art parallel
*   **Set label year:** 2023

### Community Pulse
Discussion splits cleanly into two camps that rarely overlap. The first is purely aesthetic: manga-art Luffys are collected as art objects, and threads about them fill up with framing, display and lighting talk rather than deck lists. The second is structural, and it is where the friction lives - the OP05-119 number appears across several distinct printings and label variants, so buyers routinely have to confirm which specific version a listing actually describes before acting on a price. Collectors who track this card warn newcomers that matching the card number alone is not enough, and that the set label, the border treatment and the language block all have to line up. Grading chatter follows the familiar Bandai pattern: a black-and-white field makes surface scratches and print lines more visible than a busy colour illustration would, so gem-grade outcomes are treated as harder-won here than on standard-art equivalents.

### Card Fun Facts
*   Manga-art parallels invert the usual TCG hierarchy - the plainest-looking card in a pack is frequently the most sought-after one in it.
*   The monochrome panel treatment makes centering and edge whitening unusually easy to spot with the naked eye, which is why raw copies are scrutinised so heavily before submission.
*   Because several printings share the OP05-119 number, the catalog set label does real identification work on this card rather than acting as decoration.

### Summary (TLDR)
This is Luffy rendered in manga panel art on the OP05-119 slot, collected first as artwork and second as a game piece. Its defining market quirk is identification: the same card number spans multiple printings and labels, so pinning down the exact version - and reading a surface that hides nothing - matters more than usual.
